sections.subtitle: StartupVG Masterclass: inkubator koji želi graditi zajednicu, a ne samo dijeliti znanje
sections.screenshot_description: Domagoj Ilečić otvara prvo predavanje iz serije StartupVG Masterclass
sections.content:
Večer u poduzetničkom inkubatoru **StartupVG** otvorio je njegov direktor **Domagoj Ilečić**. Predavanje s gostom **Matijom Stepanićem** prvo je u nizu masterclass predavanja. Inkubator na njih želi dovoditi vrhunske stručnjake za razvoj novih tehnologija, umjetne inteligencije i inovacija, ali i uspješne osnivače hrvatskih startupa i tehnoloških tvrtki. Ti bi gosti svoja iskustva dijelili sa zainteresiranom javnošću, a posebno s mladim startupima i novim tvrtkama.

Ilečić naglašava da serija nije zamišljena samo kao prijenos znanja. Inkubator kroz nju želi graditi ono što naziva **StartupVG zajednicom**. To je krug ljudi koji žele znati više, učiniti više i dijeliti iskustvo. Neki od njih jednoga dana mogli bi postati dio novog poduzetničkog pothvata ili startup tima, ili čak pokrenuti vlastitu brzorastuću tehnološku tvrtku.

Direktor je predstavio i kolegice iz inkubatora: **Antoniju Bakeš**, voditeljicu za pripremu i provedbu programa i projekata, te **Nikolinu Makaj**, stručnu suradnicu. Sudionike je pozvao da nakon predavanja ostanu na neformalnom druženju uz kiflice i sokove, gdje mogu postaviti pitanja o radu inkubatora.

Gosta je najavio kao „zvijezdu večeri”: vrhunskog softverskog stručnjaka i poduzetnika s mnogo iskustva u radu s AI agentima. Zahvalio mu je što je izdvojio vrijeme da s publikom podijeli svoje znanje i projekte.
sections.subtitle_en: StartupVG Masterclass: an incubator that wants to build a community, and not only share knowledge
sections.screenshot_description_en: Domagoj Ilečić opens the first lecture from the StartupVG Masterclass series
sections.content_en:
The evening at the business incubator **StartupVG** was opened by its director **Domagoj Ilečić**. The lecture with guest **Matija Stepanić** is the first in a series of masterclass lectures. The incubator wants to bring to them top experts for the development of new technologies, artificial intelligence, and innovations, but also successful founders of Croatian startups and technology companies. These guests would share their experiences with the interested public, and especially with young startups and new companies.

Ilečić emphasizes that the series is not conceived only as a transfer of knowledge. Through it, the incubator wants to build what it calls the **StartupVG community**. This is a circle of people who want to know more, do more, and share experience. Some of them could one day become part of a new business venture or startup team, or even launch their own fast-growing technology company.

The director also introduced colleagues from the incubator: **Antonija Bakeš**, head of preparation and implementation of programs and projects, and **Nikolina Makaj**, expert associate. He invited the participants to stay after the lecture for informal socializing with crescent rolls and juices, where they can ask questions about the work of the incubator.

He announced the guest as the „star of the evening”: a top software expert and entrepreneur with a lot of experience in working with AI agents. He thanked him for taking the time to share his knowledge and projects with the audience.

sections.subtitle: Dvadeset godina koda i osjećaj „drugog para ruku”
sections.screenshot_description: Matija Stepanić opisuje kako mu AI posljednje dvije godine služi kao drugi par ruku
sections.content:
Matija Stepanić predavanje je zamislio kao „interaktivni podcast”, iako u njemu ne razgovaraju samo dvije osobe. Softverskim razvojem bavi se dvadesetak godina, još od drugog razreda srednje škole 2006. godine. Kaže da je u tom razdoblju „na ruke iskodirao svašta”. Posljednje dvije godine, međutim, svaki dan ima osjećaj kao da je dobio **još jedan par ruku**.

Umjetnu inteligenciju opisuje kao tehnologiju kakvu čovječanstvo nikada prije nije imalo. Ističe i da je ona **neutralna** te se koristi kao svaki drugi alat. Nikad nije bilo lakše proizvesti laž, ali ni lakše širiti istinu. Pitanje je samo kako će je ljudi koristiti.

Promjenu u radu ilustrira vlastitim iskustvom. Za mnoge projekte o kojima je godinama sanjao nekad je trebalo osigurati financiranje u milijunima eura i okupiti tim od tridesetak ljudi koji pokrivaju sve, od prodaje i pravnih poslova do razvoja. Bio je to linearan proces na koji su svi navikli. Danas je, kaže, s AI-jem moguće otići **izravno od ideje do krajnjeg proizvoda**, a da korisnika gotovo ne zanima što se događa između, jer to „jednostavno toliko dobro radi”.

Stepanić koristi **Claude Code** od trećeg dana nakon što je alat postao dostupan u paušalnoj Claude pretplati. Publiku je pitao tko je ikad koristio Claude Code ili Claude Desktop. Ruku je podigla otprilike trećina prisutnih, pa je ostale u šali savjetovao da se upoznaju s njima.
sections.subtitle_en: Twenty years of code and the feeling of „a second pair of hands”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matija Stepanić describes how AI has been serving him as a second pair of hands for the last two years
sections.content_en:
Matija Stepanić envisioned the lecture as an „interactive podcast”, although not only two people talk in it. He has been involved in software development for about twenty years, ever since the second grade of high school in 2006. He says that in that period he „coded all sorts of things by hand”. For the last two years, however, every day he has the feeling as if he got **another pair of hands**.

He describes artificial intelligence as a technology such as humanity has never had before. He also points out that it is **neutral** and is used like any other tool. It has never been easier to produce a lie, but neither has it been easier to spread the truth. The only question is how people will use it.

He illustrates the change in work with his own experience. For many projects he had dreamed of for years, it was once necessary to secure funding in the millions of euros and assemble a team of about thirty people who cover everything, from sales and legal affairs to development. It was a linear process that everyone was used to. Today, he says, with AI it is possible to go **directly from idea to final product**, while the user is hardly interested in what happens in between, because it „simply works that well”.

Stepanić has been using **Claude Code** since the third day after the tool became available in the flat-rate Claude subscription. He asked the audience who had ever used Claude Code or Claude Desktop. Approximately a third of those present raised their hands, so he jokingly advised the others to get acquainted with them.

sections.subtitle: „Uložiš jedan, dobiješ 99”: zašto je AI danas nevjerojatno jeftin
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje subvencije za AI sa subvencijama za električne automobile
sections.content:
Stepanić objašnjava zašto su alati poput Claudea danas toliko moćni i dostupni. Ova je tehnologija, kaže, **nemjerljivo subvencionirana** od strane velikih tehnoloških kompanija. Koristi usporedbu s državnim poticajima za električne automobile, gdje kupac dobije, primjerice, 15 posto natrag. Uz napomenu da karikira brojke, procjenjuje da u AI-ju korisnik „uloži jedan, a dobije 99”.

To stanje, upozorava, neće trajati vječno. Velike kompanije poput Amazona i Googlea ulažu golem novac da se AI proširi i da ga svi koriste. Modeli se pokreću u podatkovnim centrima, a kompanije troše vlastitu struju kako bi ljude privukle da ih koriste. Prema Stepanićevim riječima, u AI industriji trenutno zarađuju gotovo isključivo **hardverske kompanije**. Prednjači **Nvidia**, koja proizvodi grafičke procesore i opremu za podatkovne centre i visoko je profitabilna. Softverske kompanije su, nasuprot tome, nisko profitabilne.

Otvara i šire društveno pitanje. U velikim jezičnim modelima nalazi se znanje cijelog čovječanstva, dostupno u svakom kutku svijeta. Ako je tako, smatra Stepanić, ovo bi stoljeće moglo pripasti **Africi**, jer će se proizvodnja hrane i svega ostalog snažno decentralizirati. Sljedeće je pitanje kako decentralizirati upravljanje likvidnošću i energijom. Ubrzavaju se i procesi poput izdavanja građevinskih dozvola, sklapanja ugovora i izrade softvera, pa jedna osoba danas može napraviti mnogo toga.

Uz konzultantske poslove, u kojima AI također koristi svakodnevno, Stepanić se svjesno pozicionirao na području koje AI ne može zamijeniti: **ondje gdje ljudi razgovaraju**. „Dok je god ljudi, ljudi će pričati”, kaže. Pitanje je samo kako AI može pomoći da se ti razgovori pametnije obrađuju.

Najveći dio onoga što radi otvorenog je koda. Poručuje da se za gotovo svaki zamislivi društveni problem ili postojeći proizvod, primjerice Revolut, uz AI razmjerno lako može napraviti vlastita kopija koja je bolja i prilagođena konkretnoj namjeni. Kao primjer pokazuje aplikaciju za automatizaciju na **e-Poreznoj**: AI mu je napisao komad JavaScripta koji automatski analizira porezno-knjigovodstvenu karticu.
sections.subtitle_en: „You invest one, you get 99”: why AI is incredibly cheap today
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares subsidies for AI with subsidies for electric cars
sections.content_en:
Stepanić explains why tools like Claude are so powerful and accessible today. This technology, he says, is **immeasurably subsidized** by large technology companies. He uses a comparison with state incentives for electric cars, where the buyer gets, for example, 15 percent back. With the note that he is caricaturing the numbers, he estimates that in AI the user „invests one, and gets 99”.

That state, he warns, will not last forever. Large companies like Amazon and Google are investing huge money so that AI spreads and everyone uses it. Models are run in data centers, and companies spend their own electricity in order to attract people to use them. According to Stepanić's words, in the AI industry currently almost exclusively **hardware companies** are making money. Leading the way is **Nvidia**, which produces graphics processors and equipment for data centers and is highly profitable. Software companies are, in contrast, low-profit.

He also opens a broader social question. In large language models is the knowledge of all humanity, available in every corner of the world. If that is so, Stepanić believes, this century could belong to **Africa**, because the production of food and everything else will be strongly decentralized. The next question is how to decentralize the management of liquidity and energy. Processes like the issuance of building permits, concluding contracts, and software development are also accelerating, so one person today can do a lot.

Along with consulting work, in which he also uses AI daily, Stepanić has consciously positioned himself in an area that AI cannot replace: **where people talk**. „As long as there are people, people will talk”, he says. The only question is how AI can help process these conversations more smartly.

Most of what he does is open source. He conveys that for almost every conceivable social problem or existing product, for example Revolut, with AI one can relatively easily make one's own copy that is better and tailored to a specific purpose. As an example, he shows an automation application on **e-Porezna**: AI wrote him a piece of JavaScript that automatically analyzes the tax accounting card.

sections.subtitle: Klijenti šalju zahtjeve u WhatsApp, a Claude ih čita: što je uopće MCP
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava kako mu klijenti šalju zahtjeve putem WhatsApp grupa
sections.content:
Stepanić kaže da bi o svojim projektima mogao pričati „jedno 14 sati, možda i više”. Zato je publiku zamolio da ga prekida i postavlja pitanja u bilo kojem trenutku. Najprije je pokazao kako izgleda njegova svakodnevna suradnja s klijentima. U publici su bili **Lucija i Marko**, koji imaju vlastite projekte i njegovi su klijenti.

Komunikacija se odvija putem **WhatsAppa**. Klijenti mu šalju zahtjeve kao screenshot, tekst ili glasovnu poruku. Stepanić je na temelju postojećih open source rješenja složio sustav koji koristi **WhatsApp bridge** i **WhatsApp MCP**. MCP pojašnjava jednostavno: to je „mali plugin za Claude”.

Klijenti mu tijekom dana, asinkrono, u tridesetak WhatsApp grupa šalju zahtjeve tipa „želim ovu promjenu, želim onu promjenu”. Ranije se komunikacija vodila mailom ili porukama, nakon čega bi se definirala i razvila nova funkcionalnost. Ovako, kaže, sve ide znatno **agilnije**. Njegov se radni dan pritom može usmjeriti na ono što najviše voli raditi posljednjih dvadeset godina: da aplikacije rade **dobro, brzo i sigurno**.

Zanimljivu je promjenu primijetio i u dizajnu. Kad bi ga netko pitao da mu napravi aplikaciju, odgovarao bi: „Jel imaš dizajnera, ja ti radim ružne aplikacije.” S AI-jem njegove aplikacije sada izgledaju pristojno. Modeli su, objašnjava, upili znanje svih programera, tekstopisaca, ali i dizajnera, pa svatko na neki način dobiva pristup svim tim vještinama.
sections.subtitle_en: Clients send requests to WhatsApp, and Claude reads them: what even is MCP
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains how clients send him requests via WhatsApp groups
sections.content_en:
Stepanić says that he could talk about his projects „about 14 hours, maybe even more”. That is why he asked the audience to interrupt him and ask questions at any moment. First, he showed what his daily collaboration with clients looks like. In the audience were **Lucija and Marko**, who have their own projects and are his clients.

Communication takes place via **WhatsApp**. Clients send him requests as a screenshot, text, or voice message. Based on existing open source solutions, Stepanić put together a system that uses **WhatsApp bridge** and **WhatsApp MCP**. He explains MCP simply: it is „a small plugin for Claude”.

During the day, asynchronously, in about thirty WhatsApp groups, clients send him requests of the type „I want this change, I want that change”. Previously, communication was conducted by email or messages, after which new functionality would be defined and developed. This way, he says, everything goes significantly **more agilely**. His workday can in the process be focused on what he loves doing most for the last twenty years: that applications work **well, fast, and securely**.

He also noticed an interesting change in design. When someone would ask him to make them an application, he would reply: „Do you have a designer, I make ugly applications for you.” With AI, his applications now look decent. The models, he explains, have absorbed the knowledge of all programmers, copywriters, but also designers, so everyone in some way gains access to all those skills.

sections.subtitle: Prvi open source contributor u Hrvatskoj i „anomalija” od 32.000 dolara
sections.screenshot_description: Na ekranu je statistika korištenja koja pokazuje prividnu potrošnju od 32.000 dolara na Claude
sections.content:
Stepanić je publici pokazao svoj „mali CV”, pregled svih vlastitih projekata. Kaže da su njegovi open source rezultati „presmiješni”: završio je na **prvom mjestu open source contributora u Hrvatskoj**. Realno bi, dodaje, trebao biti negdje na devetom mjestu, ali je javno objavio i jedan dataset, što mu je podiglo poziciju.

Zanimljiviju je „anomaliju” pokazao u statistici korištenja Claudea. Prema njoj ispada kao da je na Claude potrošio **32.000 dolara**. Stvarnost je posve drukčija: u dvije godine potrošio je manje od **2.000 eura**. Razlog je ono što se, kako kaže, pokazalo kao „best buy”, a to je **Claude Max** pretplata.

Pretplata košta oko **90 eura mjesečno**. Prema njegovim riječima, uključuje 5,5-satne sesije u kojima se može potrošiti određena količina tokena, uz poseban tjedni limit. Taj isti Claude Code dijeli s bratom i to im je dovoljno za svakodnevni rad. Ponekad istovremeno pokrene osam do deset paralelnih Claude Code sesija na različitim projektima.

Tijekom tog dijela pokazao je i jednu aktivnu sesiju te pitao je li netko iz publike već poslao poruku u WhatsApp grupu predavanja. Naglasio je da u svemu tome nema velike nove tehnologije. Sve te mogućnosti postojale su i prije AI-ja, samo se sada uz WhatsApp MCP vrlo lako može reći: „Daj mi sad pozovi tu neku funkciju.”
sections.subtitle_en: The first open source contributor in Croatia and the „anomaly” of 32,000 dollars
sections.screenshot_description_en: On the screen is usage statistics showing apparent spending of 32,000 dollars on Claude
sections.content_en:
Stepanić showed the audience his „small CV”, an overview of all his own projects. He says that his open source results are „hilarious”: he finished in **first place among open source contributors in Croatia**. Realistically, he adds, he should be somewhere in ninth place, but he also publicly published a dataset, which raised his position.

He showed a more interesting „anomaly” in the Claude usage statistics. According to it, it looks as if he spent **32,000 dollars** on Claude. The reality is completely different: in two years he spent less than **2,000 euros**. The reason is what, as he says, turned out to be a „best buy”, and that is the **Claude Max** subscription.

The subscription costs around **90 euros per month**. According to his words, it includes 5.5-hour sessions in which a certain amount of tokens can be spent, with a special weekly limit. He shares that same Claude Code with his brother, and that is enough for them for daily work. Sometimes he simultaneously runs eight to ten parallel Claude Code sessions on different projects.

During that part, he also showed an active session and asked if someone from the audience had already sent a message to the lecture's WhatsApp group. He emphasized that in all of this there is no big new technology. All these capabilities existed even before AI, it's just that now with WhatsApp MCP it is very easy to say: „Call that function for me now.”

sections.subtitle: Claude Code bez ikakvih dopuštenja: „Može vam obrisati disk”
sections.screenshot_description: Gost u terminalu pokazuje kako pokreće Claude Code s opcijom preskakanja dopuštenja
sections.content:
Stepanić je pokazao kako pokreće Claude Code na računalu: iz terminala, s opcijom koju naziva **„dangerously skip permissions”**. Kaže da je tako koristi otkako koristi Claude, iako to, prema njegovoj procjeni, ne radi 99,9 posto korisnika.

Posljedice ne skriva. Program na računalu tada doslovno može raditi sve: **obrisati disk, poslati mail u korisnikovo ime**, izvršiti bilo kakvu radnju. Zašto onda riskira? Stepanić razmišlja ovako: najveći investitori u Anthropic su Amazon i Google. Te kompanije ne žele svjetski skandal, pa očekuje da su taj softver razvile vrlo sigurno. Smatra da oni o sigurnosti vode više računa nego što su programeri godinama vodili o raznim rubnim slučajevima.

Objašnjava i što se zapravo događa u terminalu. Riječ je o malom programu koji razmjenjuje poruke, pamti što je korisnik radio i poziva pravi model, primjerice **Opus 5.5**. Model se nalazi na Amazonovim serverima ili u velikom podatkovnom centru Elona Muska u **Memphisu**. Ondje je, kaže, hardver vrijedan oko 50 milijardi dolara. Komad teksta napisan u terminalu vrlo vjerojatno putuje u Memphis i obrađuje se na serveru vrijednom oko dva milijuna dolara.

Dodaje da bi takav softver, i kad bi se pokretao u malom lokalnom podatkovnom centru, trošio jako mnogo struje. Upravo zato smatra da je današnji rad s AI-jem subvencioniran na golemoj skali.
sections.subtitle_en: Claude Code without any permissions: „It can wipe your disk”
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest in the terminal shows how he runs Claude Code with the option of skipping permissions
sections.content_en:
Stepanić showed how he runs Claude Code on the computer: from the terminal, with the option he calls **„dangerously skip permissions”**. He says that he has been using it that way since he has been using Claude, although, according to his estimate, 99.9 percent of users do not do that.

He does not hide the consequences. The program on the computer can then literally do everything: **wipe the disk, send an email in the user's name**, execute any action. Why then does he take the risk? Stepanić thinks like this: the biggest investors in Anthropic are Amazon and Google. Those companies do not want a worldwide scandal, so he expects that they developed that software very securely. He considers that they pay more attention to security than programmers have paid for years to various edge cases.

He also explains what actually happens in the terminal. It is a small program that exchanges messages, remembers what the user did, and calls the real model, for example **Opus 5.5**. The model is located on Amazon's servers or in Elon Musk's large data center in **Memphis**. There, he says, is hardware worth around 50 billion dollars. A piece of text written in the terminal most likely travels to Memphis and is processed on a server worth about two million dollars.

Dodaje da bi takav softver, i kad bi se pokretao u malom lokalnom podatkovnom centru, trošio jako mnogo struje. Upravo zato smatra da je današnji rad s AI-jem subvencioniran na golemoj skali.

sections.subtitle: Alat koji radi alate: vlastiti AutoCAD, studio za podcaste i kopija Netflixa
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prikazuje macOS aplikaciju Domovina Studio za snimanje podcasta
sections.content:
Zašto je AI najveća revolucija koju je itko vidio? Stepanić odgovara u jednoj rečenici: zato što je to **„alat koji radi alate”**. Uz Claude si, kaže, svatko može napraviti vlastiti AutoCAD, Photoshop ili Word, ili bilo što drugo što mu padne na pamet.

Navodi primjer iz privatnog života. Kod **parcelacije zemlje** u Claude se ubaci DWG datoteka koju vrati geodet, zatraži se izrada poligona za konkretan slučaj, a Claude uz pomoć raznih biblioteka napravi malu web aplikaciju.

Pokazao je i **Domovina Studio**, macOS aplikaciju koju mu je Claude napravio za snimanje podcasta. Prilagođena je točno hardveru u njegovu uredu: kameri i mikrofonima. Aplikacija:
- automatski radi **lipsync** kada kamera kasni 600 milisekundi, uz pomoć raznih Python skripti;
- u slučaju nestanka struje ili interneta snimke automatski sprema na **Cloudflare R2**.

Cloudflare R2 je, objašnjava, usluga za vrlo jeftino pohranjivanje datoteka u Cloudflareovu oblaku. Posebna je po tome što je trenutno jedina u svijetu koja **ne naplaćuje internetski promet** kada netko preuzima datoteke. Zato se uz nju može napraviti vlastiti streaming servis, kopija YouTubea ili Netflixa. Upravo tako nastao je **Domovina AI**, na kojem se trenutno nalazi više od 3.000 podcast epizoda, odnosno tristotinjak gigabajta datoteka.

Pokazao je i koliko se danas sve može decentralizirati. Spojio se na udaljeno računalo s dva monitora u uredu u **Lomnici**, preko alata **RustDesk**. Ondje je pustio video u kojem **Don Antun** recenzira **Magisterijum AI**, hostan također na Cloudflare R2. To je, kaže, samo jedan od ukupno **102 projekta**.
sections.subtitle_en: A tool that makes tools: one's own AutoCAD, a podcast studio and a copy of Netflix
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest shows the macOS application Domovina Studio for recording podcasts
sections.content_en:
Why is AI the greatest revolution that anyone has seen? Stepanić answers in one sentence: because it is **„a tool that makes tools”**.

He cites an example from private life. In **land subdivision**, a DWG file returned by the surveyor is inserted into Claude, the creation of a polygon for the specific case is requested, and Claude, with the help of various libraries, makes a small web application.

He also showed **Domovina Studio**, a macOS application that Claude made for him for recording podcasts. It is tailored exactly to the hardware in his office: the camera and microphones. The application:
- automatically does **lipsync** when the camera lags 600 milliseconds, with the help of various Python scripts;
- in case of a power or internet outage, automatically saves recordings to **Cloudflare R2**.

Cloudflare R2 is, he explains, a service for very cheap file storage in Cloudflare's cloud. It is special in that it is currently the only one in the world that **does not charge for internet traffic** when someone downloads files. That is why, with it, one can make one's own streaming service, a copy of YouTube or Netflix. That is precisely how **Domovina AI** was created, on which there are currently more than 3,000 podcast episodes, that is, about three hundred gigabytes of files.

He also showed how much everything can be decentralized today. He connected to a remote computer with two monitors in the office in **Lomnica**, via the **RustDesk** tool. There he played a video in which **Don Antun** reviews **Magisterijum AI**, also hosted on Cloudflare R2. That is, he says, only one of a total of **102 projects**.

sections.subtitle: Lovable i ostali posrednici: zašto je dovoljan samo Claude Code
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava ekonomiku platformi poput Lovablea koje preprodaju Claude Code
sections.content:
Stepanić je publiku pitao je li netko koristio **Lovable** ili sličnog AI asistenta. Lovable je, kaže, „fora”, ali je zapravo riječ o svojevrsnoj veleprodaji. Lovable je izgradio aplikaciju koja interno koristi **Claude Code SDK**, a dodao je Supabase, lijepu izradu web-stranica i druge mogućnosti.

Računica ide otprilike ovako: korisnik plati jedan dolar za određenu količinu tokena, zadatak se izvršava pet do šest minuta, a Lovable Anthropicu za API plati oko 36 centi. Dio ide Supabaseu, a ostatak je njihov dio kolača. Stepanić dodaje da takve kompanije trenutno žive od investicija, pa se događa i da korisnik plati dolar, a oni sedam, samo kako bi širili korisničku bazu.

Njegov je zaključak, potvrđen u praksi: **ne treba ništa osim Claude Codea**, jer nema daljnjeg posrednika. Claude Code je proizvod Anthropica, a isti proizvođač radi i jezični model. Taj se model pokreće u podatkovnim centrima Amazona i SpaceX-a.

Stepanić objašnjava i što Claude Code zapravo radi. Model prima komad teksta, troši struju i vraća komad teksta, primjerice HTML kontakt-forme. Claude Code pritom **u petlji** poziva model, provjerava rezultat, uočava grešku i ponovno poziva model, sve dok korisnik ne dobije ispravan odgovor. Korisnik napiše upit samo jednom, a u pozadini se model poziva više puta. Taj sustav pravila koja drže model pod kontrolom u AI svijetu naziva se **harness**.

Na kraju se dotaknuo i infrastrukture. Prema njegovim riječima, Anthropic SpaceX-u za najam podatkovnog centra koji je Elon Musk izgradio za gotovo 50 milijardi dolara plaća **1,25 milijardi dolara mjesečno**, a Google je ostatak iznajmio za 920 milijuna. Centar je pod punim opterećenjem i potpuno iznajmljen. Jedan takav podatkovni centar želi se izgraditi i u **Topuskom**, a u Americi ih se navodno paralelno gradi petnaestak. Otvoreno pitanje ostaje koliko će struje sve to trošiti.
sections.subtitle_en: Lovable and other intermediaries: why only Claude Code is enough
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains the economics of platforms like Lovable that resell Claude Code
sections.content_en:
Stepanić asked the audience whether anyone had used **Lovable** or a similar AI assistant. Lovable is, he says, „cool”, but it is actually a matter of a kind of wholesale. Lovable built an application that internally uses the **Claude Code SDK**, and added Supabase, nice website creation, and other capabilities.

The calculation goes roughly like this: the user pays one dollar for a certain amount of tokens, the task runs for five to six minutes, and Lovable pays Anthropic about 36 cents for the API. Part goes to Supabase, and the rest is their slice of the pie. Stepanić adds that such companies currently live off investments, so it also happens that the user pays a dollar and they pay seven, just to expand the user base.

His conclusion, confirmed in practice: **nothing is needed except Claude Code**, because there is no further intermediary. Claude Code is a product of Anthropic, and the same manufacturer also makes the language model. That model runs in the data centers of Amazon and SpaceX.

Stepanić also explains what Claude Code actually does. The model receives a piece of text, consumes electricity, and returns a piece of text, for example the HTML of a contact form. In doing so, Claude Code calls the model **in a loop**, checks the result, notices an error, and calls the model again, until the user gets a correct response. The user writes a query only once, and in the background the model is called multiple times. That system of rules that keep the model under control is called a **harness** in the AI world.

In the end, he also touched upon infrastructure. According to his words, Anthropic pays SpaceX **1.25 billion dollars per month** for the lease of the data center that Elon Musk built for nearly 50 billion dollars, and Google leased the rest for 920 million. The center is under full load and fully leased. One such data center is also sought to be built in **Topusko**, and in America about fifteen of them are allegedly being built in parallel. An open question remains how much electricity all of that will consume.

sections.subtitle: Uživo: Claude čita poruke publike i odgovara hrvatskom zastavom
sections.screenshot_description: Claude u terminalu čita poruke iz WhatsApp grupe predavanja i šalje odgovor
sections.content:
Uslijedila je prva demonstracija uživo. Stepanić je Claudeu zadao da provjeri ima li novih poruka u WhatsApp grupi predavanja. Claude je javio da WhatsApp pošiljatelje prikazuje samo kao brojeve, pa ne zna kako se zovu. Pitanja još nema, samo pozdravi, i ponudio je da im odgovori. Stepanić mu je rekao da odgovori **emojijem hrvatske zastave**. Poruka „Pozdrav i dobrodošli” stigla je sudionicima u grupi, što je jedan od njih i potvrdio.

Tijekom demonstracije upozorio je na jednu zanimljivost. Anthropic zarađuje prodajom tokena, pa Claude Code stalno predlaže nove korake i upite kojima bi korisnik potrošio još tokena. U nekom trenutku prijedlozi postanu očito nepotrebni, i tada čovjek mora odlučiti: „Sad je dosta, idemo dalje.” Na ekranu se pritom vidjela potrošnja tokena dok program poziva endpoint modela u podatkovnom centru.

Primijetio je i sitnu grešku: Claude Code još ne prikazuje ispravno sadržaj kada korisnik zumira. „Nek si oni to poprave”, dobacio je. Dodao je i podatak koji smatra fascinantnim: ekipa u Anthropicu **razvija Claude Code uz pomoć Claude Codea**. To je, kaže, svojevrsna beskonačna petlja. Vjerojatno smo došli do točke u kojoj je produktivnost premašila potrebni ulog, pa je moguće napraviti gotovo sve.
sections.subtitle_en: Live: Claude reads the audience's messages and responds with the Croatian flag
sections.screenshot_description_en: Claude in the terminal reads messages from the lecture WhatsApp group and sends a response
sections.content_en:
The first live demonstration followed. Stepanić tasked Claude to check whether there are new messages in the lecture WhatsApp group. Claude reported that WhatsApp displays senders only as numbers, so it does not know what they are called. There are no questions yet, only greetings, and it offered to reply to them. Stepanić told it to respond with the **Croatian flag emoji**. The message „Greetings and welcome” arrived to the participants in the group, which one of them also confirmed.

During the demonstration, he pointed out an interesting detail. Anthropic makes money by selling tokens, so Claude Code constantly suggests new steps and queries with which the user would spend more tokens. At some point, the suggestions become obviously unnecessary, and then a person must decide: „Now it's enough, let's move on.” On the screen, token consumption was visible at the same time while the program calls the model's endpoint in the data center.

He also noticed a minor bug: Claude Code does not yet display content correctly when the user zooms in. „Let them fix that themselves”, he quipped. He also added a fact that he considers fascinating: the team at Anthropic **develops Claude Code with the help of Claude Code**. That is, he says, a kind of infinite loop. We have probably reached the point where productivity has exceeded the required input, so it is possible to make almost anything.

sections.subtitle: Web-stranica tvrtke na zahtjev publike: od tipfelera do gotovog koda
sections.screenshot_description: Gost upisuje prompt za izradu web-stranice tvrtke s kontakt-formom
sections.content:
U WhatsApp grupi stiglo je prvo konkretno pitanje iz publike: može li se napraviti jednostavna informativna web-stranica neke tvrtke s kontakt-formom ili je to previše složeno? Stepanić je odgovorio potvrdno i odmah upisao prompt. Tražio je od Claudea da složi plan bez previše kompliciranja, napravi samo korisničko sučelje i rad provjerava sam, uz **Claude in Chrome** u pregledniku **Brave** i **Claude Vision**, u petlji verifikacije. Sve je trebalo raditi u zasebnom folderu, uz stabilne commitove malo po malo.

Publika je mogla vidjeti da je prompt pun tipfelera. To ne smeta, objašnjava Stepanić: ono što korisnik napiše, pa i sa slovnim greškama, golema istrenirana neuronska mreža prepoznaje kao vrlo slično onome što je mislio. Uskoro se pojavila datoteka `index.html` s demo stranicom izmišljene tvrtke **Stolarija Lipa iz Velike Gorice**, a Claude je u Pythonu pokrenuo mali HTTP server.

Stepanić naglašava da Claudeu nije rekao koju tehnologiju koristi. Modeli velikih kompanija, primjećuje, najčešće posežu za Pythonom na backendu i Reactom na frontendu. Programski su jezici danas, smatra, postali nebitni. Može se pisati na hrvatskom, a model razumije i na engleskom ili slovenskom. Jednako tako kod iz Pythona prepisuje u JavaScript, Node.js ili Rust. Sve je to „pametno prepisivanje”.

Prava vrijednost Claude Codea, prema Stepaniću, jest u tome što koristi **stare, provjerene alate**. Program je oduvijek morao biti sintaksno ispravan da bi se dao kompajlirati. Claude se na računalu pokrene i, ako naiđe na grešku, šalje je modelu, koji je ispravi. Proces se vrti dok korisnik ne dobije funkcionalnu aplikaciju.

Priznaje da terminal izgleda „dosta ružno”, ali mu je najpraktičniji jer je tako najbliže proizvođaču modela. Lovable nudi lijepo sučelje i ne zahtijeva nikakvu instalaciju: u pregledniku se otvori novi projekt i sve se odradi.
sections.subtitle_en: Company website at the audience's request: from typos to finished code
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest enters a prompt for creating a company website with a contact form
sections.content_en:
In the WhatsApp group, the first concrete question from the audience arrived: can a simple informative website of a company with a contact form be made, or is that too complex? Stepanić answered affirmatively and immediately entered a prompt. He asked Claude to put together a plan without overcomplicating, make only the user interface, and verify the work itself, with **Claude in Chrome** in the **Brave** browser and **Claude Vision**, in a verification loop. Everything was supposed to be done in a separate folder, with stable commits little by little.

The audience could see that the prompt was full of typos. That does not matter, Stepanić explains: what the user writes, even with spelling errors, a massive trained neural network recognizes as very similar to what he meant. Soon the file `index.html` appeared with a demo page of the fictional company **Stolarija Lipa from Velika Gorica**, and Claude started a small HTTP server in Python.

Stepanić emphasizes that he did not tell Claude which technology to use. Models of large companies, he notes, most often reach for Python on the backend and React on the frontend. Programming languages today, he believes, have become irrelevant. One can write in Croatian, and the model understands in English or Slovenian as well. Likewise, it rewrites code from Python into JavaScript, Node.js, or Rust. All of that is „smart rewriting”.

The true value of Claude Code, according to Stepanić, is that it uses **old, proven tools**. A program has always had to be syntactically correct in order to be compiled. Claude starts on the computer and, if it encounters an error, sends it to the model, which corrects it. The process loops until the user gets a functional application.

He admits that the terminal looks „quite ugly”, but it is the most practical for him because that way he is closest to the model manufacturer. Lovable offers a nice interface and does not require any installation: a new project is opened in the browser and everything is done.

sections.subtitle: Claude in Chrome: AI sam klika po pregledniku i provjerava vlastiti rad
sections.screenshot_description: U pregledniku Brave vidi se virtualni miš kojim Claude testira demo stranicu
sections.content:
Dok je stranica nastajala, Stepanić je pokazao jednu od, kako kaže, „totalno cool” mogućnosti. Riječ je o službenoj ekstenziji koju Anthropic izrađuje za Chrome, a radi i u preglednicima temeljenima na Chromiumu, poput **Bravea** kojim se on služi.

Ekstenzija ima ovlasti čitati sadržaj s diska i u pregledniku dodaje vlastiti **virtualni miš**. Pomiče ga po stranici i šalje programske klikove, testirajući ono što je napravila. U vrhu preglednika stvara posebnu grupu kartica i po potrebi otvara jednu ili više njih. Demo stranica Stolarije Lipe nakon toga je bila gotova i provjerena.

Mogućnosti je ilustrirao zadatkom iz istoga dana. Za klijenta je radio aplikaciju koja prima audio ulaz. Nakon što su se dogovorili oko izgleda i gumba, Claudeu je naložio da otvori zasebnu karticu, ode na YouTube, pokrene prijenos **saborske televizije** uživo i taj zvuk koristi kao ulaz. Claude je sam kliknuo „play” u jednoj kartici i „kreni” u drugoj.

Na taj se način, objašnjava Stepanić, simulira stvarno korištenje programa. Model koji proizvodi kod uz Claude in Chrome sam klika po aplikaciji i vraća screenshotove. Ručno testiranje tako dobrim dijelom preuzima sam AI.
sections.subtitle_en: Claude in Chrome: AI itself clicks around the browser and checks its own work
sections.screenshot_description_en: In the Brave browser, a virtual mouse can be seen with which Claude tests the demo page
sections.content_en:
While the page was being created, Stepanić showed one of, as he says, „totally cool” capabilities. It is an official extension that Anthropic is developing for Chrome, and it also works in browsers based on Chromium, like **Brave** which he uses.

The extension has permissions to read content from disk and adds its own **virtual mouse** in the browser. It moves it around the page and sends programmatic clicks, testing what it has made. At the top of the browser, it creates a special group of tabs and opens one or more of them as needed. The demo page of Stolarija Lipe was after that finished and verified.

He illustrated the capabilities with a task from the same day. For a client, he was making an application that receives audio input. After they agreed on the appearance and buttons, he instructed Claude to open a separate tab, go to YouTube, start the live broadcast of **Saborska televizija** and use that sound as input. Claude himself clicked „play” in one tab and „start” in the other.

In this way, Stepanić explains, the actual use of the program is simulated. The model that produces code with Claude in Chrome clicks around the application on its own and returns screenshots. Manual testing is thus largely taken over by the AI itself.

sections.subtitle: Git kao sigurnosna mreža i zašto Claude Code smije raditi bez pitanja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost pita publiku tko zna što je Git dok Claude prijavljuje četiri commita
sections.content:
Claude je javio da je stranica gotova, da je svaki korak provjerio u Braveu i da lokalno radi, te da je napravio **četiri commita**. Stepanić je publiku pitao tko zna što je Git, a ruku je podiglo šest-sedam programera.

Git je objasnio i onima bez programerskog iskustva. Riječ je o alatu koji je izmislio **Linus Torvalds**, tvorac Linuxa. Linux i Git su, kaže, „dva alata koja vam ikad trebaju”, napravljena kao potpuno otvoreni kod za opće dobro. Git verzionira datoteke. Ako netko napiše „jabuka” i to commita, a zatim napiše „jabuka je crvena”, Git zabilježi da je stari redak obrisan i dodan novi. Kroz tu se povijest može slobodno šetati. Kada Claude koristi takve godinama provjerene alate, rezultat je, kaže, „ovakva eksplozija”.

Ključna je poruka da se korisnici trebaju ohrabriti i Claude Code pokretati bez traženja dopuštenja. Inače bi ga u ovakvom procesu tridesetak puta pitao je li siguran da želi izvršiti neku radnju. Stepanić je primijetio da stalno samo pritišće „može”, a nijedan prijedlog dosad nije bio „obrisat ću ti sve s diska”.

Primjećuje i da Anthropic, razvijajući Claude Code uz pomoć Claudea, sve više ugrađuje zaštitu od samog alata. U novijim automatskim ažuriranjima upozorenje iskače čak i kad Claude želi obrisati privremenu datoteku koju je sam napravio. Pita je li korisnik siguran i daje mu 60 sekundi, nakon čega sam odabire „ne”. Zato smatra da je alat **defenzivniji** nego što bi bio itko tko radi zlonamjerno.

Ne tvrdi da se problemi ne događaju. Bilo je slučajeva brisanja bitnih datoteka i mnogo objava o tome kako je „AI pobjegao iz sandboxa”. On Claude namjerno nikad ne pokreće u sandboxu, kako bi na disku mogao raditi što god treba. To znači da računalo mora biti **isključivo radni stroj**, na koji ne treba stavljati ništa što korisnik ne želi da AI pokupi. Pritom smatra da velike kompanije ionako već odavno, i prije AI-ja, znaju sve o nama.
sections.subtitle_en: Git as a safety net and why Claude Code is allowed to work without asking
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest asks the audience who knows what Git is while Claude reports four commits
sections.content_en:
Claude reported that the page is finished, that he checked every step in Brave and that it works locally, and that he made **four commits**. Stepanić asked the audience who knows what Git is, and six to seven programmers raised their hands.

He explained Git also to those without programming experience. It is a tool invented by **Linus Torvalds**, the creator of Linux. Linux and Git are, he says, „two tools you will ever need”, made as completely open source for the common good. Git versions files. If someone writes „apple” and commits that, and then writes „apple is red”, Git records that the old line was deleted and a new one added. Through that history, one can freely walk. When Claude uses such tools tested over the years, the result is, he says, „an explosion like this”.

The key message is that users should take courage and run Claude Code without asking for permission. Otherwise, in a process like this, it would ask him about thirty times whether he is sure he wants to execute an action. Stepanić noticed that he constantly just presses „sure”, and not a single suggestion so far has been „I will delete everything from your disk”.

He also notes that Anthropic, developing Claude Code with the help of Claude, is increasingly building in protection against the tool itself. In newer automatic updates, a warning pops up even when Claude wants to delete a temporary file that it created itself. It asks whether the user is sure and gives him 60 seconds, after which it selects „no” on its own. Therefore, he considers that the tool is **more defensive** than anyone acting maliciously would be.

He does not claim that problems do not occur. There have been cases of deleting important files and many posts about how „AI escaped from the sandbox”. He intentionally never runs Claude in a sandbox, so that it can do whatever is needed on the disk. This means that the computer must be **exclusively a work machine**, on which nothing should be placed that the user does not want AI to pick up. At the same time, he considers that big companies anyway have long known, even before AI, everything about us.

sections.subtitle: Promptati na hrvatskom ili engleskom? „Njemu je to semantički jabuka”
sections.screenshot_description: Sudionik iz publike pita daje li prompt na engleskom drukčije rezultate od prompta na hrvatskom
sections.content:
Jedan od sudionika iz publike pitao je hoće li rezultati biti drukčiji ako se prompt napiše na engleskom umjesto na hrvatskom. Stepanić kaže da sam gotovo stalno prompta na hrvatskom. Kad mu Claude počne odgovarati na engleskom, kaže mu da prestane i nastavi na hrvatskom.

Objašnjava da su neuronske mreže uglavnom istrenirane na engleskom pa **troše manje struje** kada su i ulaz i izlaz na engleskom, među ostalim zbog duljine znakova. Sam je prompt, međutim, u biti isti. Model interno razumije da su „jabuka” i „apple” semantički ista stvar. Svejedno je napiše li se „napravi formu na web-stranici” ili „create a contact form on website”.

Sudionik je zaključio da je za svakodnevne zadatke hrvatski dovoljan. Za složenije stvari, poput istraživanja ili doktorata o nečemu što još ne postoji, preporučio je engleski. Stepanić se načelno složio, ali je dodao da je i sam izlaz kao znanje semantički jednak na oba jezika.

Najčešći problem, prema njegovu iskustvu, jest to da model radi doslovne prijevode i „englizira” hrvatski tekst. Tada mu kaže otprilike ovo: sviđa mi se znanje koje si dao, ali ga napiši u duhu hrvatskog jezika, gramatički i pravopisno ispravno. Model tada preslaže rečenice: značenje ostaje isto, ali su ljepše napisane. Stepanić 99 posto posla radi na hrvatskom. Upravo je dan ranije primijetio da je Claude odjednom počeo sve ispisivati na engleskom, pa ga je morao vratiti na hrvatski.
sections.subtitle_en: Prompting in Croatian or English? „To it, that is semantically an apple”
sections.screenshot_description_en: A participant from the audience asks whether a prompt in English gives different results from a prompt in Croatian
sections.content_en:
One of the participants from the audience asked whether the results would be different if the prompt is written in English instead of in Croatian. Stepanić says that he himself almost constantly prompts in Croatian. When Claude starts answering him in English, he tells it to stop and continue in Croatian.

He explains that neural networks are mostly trained in English, so they **consume less electricity** when both input and output are in English, among other things due to character length. The prompt itself, however, is essentially the same. The model internally understands that „jabuka” and „apple” are semantically the same thing. It makes no difference whether one writes „make a form on a website” or „create a contact form on website”.

The participant concluded that for everyday tasks, Croatian is sufficient. For more complex things, like research or a doctorate about something that does not yet exist, he recommended English. Stepanić agreed in principle, but added that the output itself as knowledge is semantically equal in both languages.

The most common problem, according to his experience, is that the model makes literal translations and „anglicizes” Croatian text. Then he tells it roughly this: I like the knowledge you gave, but write it in the spirit of the Croatian language, grammatically and orthographically correct. The model then rearranges the sentences: the meaning remains the same, but they are more beautifully written. Stepanić does 99 percent of the work in Croatian. Just the day before, he noticed that Claude had suddenly started writing everything in English, so he had to return it to Croatian.
